title.narrative: Supporting the Shift to Electric Mobility in Senegal

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Supporting the development of e-mobility in Senegal to reduce GHG emissions and energy consumption, improve air quality and increase the efficiency of transport sector, with attention to long-term environmental sustainability

The project contributes to improve air quality conditions in the medium-long term, with tangible benefits on citizen’s health and quality of life; this is particularly relevant in urban environments, where traffic congestion exacerbates this negative impact, with large numbers of people exposed to health-damaging pollutants. This is particularly true for Senegal and its capital Dakar where a large number of old and poorly maintained diesel cars and minibuses mainly imported from France, Belgium and other parts of Europe contribute to extreme levels of air pollution – a problem which is amplified by the high level of congestion observed in the spatially constrained city of Dakar. Marginalized groups, who are the most exposed to polluted air, will particularly benefit from improved air quality, including for what regards lower healthcare costs. By strengthening technical competences in the different domains of the e-mobility, the project also enables the country to exploit future economic opportunities linked to the possible emergence of new activities such as EV charging, production and assembly of EVs (in particular buses based on the experience and capacity of Senbus) as well as re-use and recycling of EV batteries and components. Moreover, this allows to better prepare for the transition of technicians working in ‘traditional’ activities such as ICE vehicle maintenance. By fostering the development of the EV sector, the project will create new job opportunities in new areas such as EV maintenance, battery recycling and local EV production. This diversification will contribute to economic resilience and poverty alleviation. Mobility of persons and goods is a key enabling factor to economic growth. As such, the need for efficient public transport systems, individual mobility and the transport of goods is largely unaffected by political preferences. Whether or not Senegal will switch to electric mobility is also going to be largely determined by factors outside the country – for example the rate at which developed countries in the global north switch to electric mobility and export used EVs to global south countries such as Senegal. Lastly, and as demonstrated by the company operating the electric BRT in Dakar, the decision to shift to electric vehicles is mainly based on economic considerations – with the technology becoming more and mainstreamed, and with more and more vehicles available on the market, commercial operations will anticipate the longer-term savings offered by e-mobility and therefore take-up the technology. With Senegal not being an oil producing country, the long-term savings of using locally generated low-carbon electricity for electric mobility (with the potential of using local natural gas resources as a bridging technology) versus the importation of expensive and price-volatile petroleum fuels for which hard USD foreign exchange will need to be generated to fuel polluting ICE vehicles, will greatly contribute to overall resilience of the Senegalese economy to external shocks. This clear long-term path is also adding to the resilience of the project itself. In addition, diversification of energy trajectories will also increase short term resilience of the Senegalese transport sector for example with regards to extreme weather events and its impact on the global fossil fuel market. Lastly, the project will incorporate all necessary actions to ensure whatever that any investments in rolling stock and infrastructure will be done in a climate resilient way, for example anticipating extreme weather events such as heavy rains and subsequent flooding.
